sections.h2: Where is Arvada and how big is it?
sections.html:
Arvada is a home rule city about 7 miles northwest of the Colorado State Capitol in Denver, mostly in Jefferson County with a small part in Adams County. It covers about 39.6 square miles at an elevation near 5,500 feet.

The 2020 census counted 124,402 residents, which made Arvada the seventh largest city in Colorado, and a 2024 estimate put it at 121,873. Nearly all of them (121,510) live on the Jefferson County side, so most Arvada sellers deal with the Jefferson County Assessor and Treasurer.

The city is mostly residential, with some light industry and professional offices. Main commercial streets are Wadsworth Boulevard, Ralston Road and Kipling Street.

sections.h2: What is the history of Arvada?
sections.html:
Arvada began as a farming and gold rush area. Lewis Ralston documented gold near Ralston Creek in 1850, and the Colorado Central Railroad reached the area in 1870.

The townsite was platted on December 1, 1870, as Ralston Point and renamed Arvada, after Hiram Arvada Haskin, the brother-in-law of settler Mary Wadsworth. The town incorporated in 1904, became a statutory city in 1951 and a home rule municipality in 1963.

  • Pascal celery earned Arvada the nickname Celery Capital of the World in the early 1900s.
  • Colorado's first supermarket opened here in 1947.
  • The Rocky Flats Plant, which made nuclear weapon triggers, ran from 1952 to 1992 just outside the city, and the Rocky Flats National Wildlife Refuge is now nearby.

A lot of Arvada housing dates from the post World War II suburban boom, so ranch homes with original systems are common listings.

sections.h2: Which parts of Arvada do buyers and sellers talk about?
sections.html:
Olde Town Arvada is the historic core, with shops, restaurants and a transit hub. Around it sit older neighborhoods with smaller lots, while newer subdivisions spread toward the edges of the city.

Homes near a G Line station tend to be marketed around the commute, and the Arvada Center for the Arts and Humanities draws visitors to the city.

sections.h2: What is the weather like, and what does it mean for an Arvada house?
sections.html:
Arvada has a humid continental climate, with an average annual precipitation of about 16 inches and the wettest months in spring and summer. The mean annual high is about 65.7 degrees and the mean low about 37.1.

Front Range spring storms are the usual test for roofs, gutters and windows. Buyers who inspect an older Arvada house will look closely at roof age, drainage near the foundation and the furnace, and those are the items that sellers tend to price in or repair.

Ask your insurance agent what your policy says about hail and wind before you list, because an open claim can complicate a closing.

sections.h2: What are Arvada's short-term rental rules?
sections.html:
Arvada allows short-term rentals of less than 30 days with a city license. At a February 2025 council workshop, staff said the city had more than 800 short-term rentals and only about 250 to 300 were licensed, and that the annual registration fee was $150.

A house that was used as a short-term rental may carry unresolved licensing or complaint history, so buyers sometimes ask for proof. If you are selling an Arvada property that was rented to guests, gather the license, any city notices and tax filings first.

sections.h2: How does property tax work for Arvada homeowners?
sections.html:
Jefferson County values the property, and the Jefferson County Treasurer collects the tax. The Treasurer's office is at 100 Jefferson County Parkway, Suite 2520, in Golden, and the phone is 303-271-8330.

  • Taxes above $25 are due in full by April 30 or in two halves, the first by the last day of February and the second by June 15.
  • For 2026 the state guide lists residential assessment rates of 6.8% for local governments and 7.05% for schools.
  • Real property is revalued in odd numbered years, and valuation notices go out by May 1.
  • Protest deadline: June 8 under the standard state schedule.

A tax lien attaches to every county property with taxes owing on January 1 each year. If the owner has not paid by late October, the county sells the lien at its annual sale, and the owner then has three years to redeem it. The Treasurer's office is closed on Fridays.

sections.h2: What are your options for selling a house in Arvada?
sections.html:
You can list with an agent, sell it yourself, or accept a cash offer for the house as is. Listing usually brings repairs, showings and weeks of waiting on a buyer's loan.

A cash sale suits sellers with an inherited house, a vacant rental, deferred repairs or a tight deadline. The deed is recorded with the county clerk, and any tax owing is paid from the proceeds. We can look at your Arvada address and explain the choices before you commit to anything.

faqs.a: Most of Arvada lies in Jefferson County, and a small part (2,892 residents in 2020) is in Adams County. Your tax bill shows which county applies.

faqs.q: What is the Arvada property tax protest deadline?
faqs.a: Under the standard state schedule the protest deadline is June 8. Read your own Notice of Valuation, since counties can use an alternate schedule.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Arvada house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Back taxes are paid from the proceeds at closing, and the title company gets the exact figure from the Jefferson County Treasurer.

faqs.q: Are short-term rentals allowed in Arvada?
faqs.a: Yes, with a license. The annual fee was reported at $150 in early 2025, and officials said many rentals were unlicensed.
Jefferson County School District R-1 serves the Jefferson County part, and Westminster Public Schools serves the Adams County part.
